limitations: This was a query-led scan of the four named institutional clusters, not exhaustive pagination of every agency catalogue or every document containing an embedded AI passage.

EASA download gateways returned HTTP 429 during this pass. Exact official download targets and publication landing pages were recorded, but the two Issue 2 PDFs should be re-opened before canonical admission to verify cover-level identifiers and dates.

EBA landing pages and one report PDF intermittently returned HTTP 403. The 2021 discussion-paper PDF itself was opened and read; the 2023 follow-up remains a known-backlog verification based on official publication/search metadata and previously recorded official indexed text.

The EMA English news extractor omitted the date header for the multi-annual AI workplan, while an exact-page search result and an archived print of that official page showed 18 December 2023. Re-capture the English page's visible metadata before admission.
The EDA AI Action Plan and Strategic Research Agenda are mentioned by official EDA material, but no independently citable public full text was found; neither is promoted as a candidate here.
Press/news pages are used only as release, role, or date evidence when they link or identify a standalone document; they are not counted as document substitutes.

The earlier gap work signposted EASA concept papers generically while itemising Roadmaps 1.0 and 2.0. The two Issue 2 rows here are newly itemised version records, not a claim that the EASA concept-paper thematic direction was wholly unseen.
Dates retain their meanings. Null document_date values are not filled from a publication-page timestamp, and the EDA CARD adoption date is not silently converted into a publication date.
Sector and provenance values are editorial proposals using the existing controlled vocabulary; they still require normal canonical review.

records.title: EASA Artificial Intelligence Concept Paper Issue 2: Guidance for Level 1 & 2 machine-learning applications
records.evidence_locator: Official general-publication page: title/subtitle; Publication Date 06/03/2024; description paragraphs 1-2; quoting-this-report block. The page identifies the linked PDF as Issue 2 and describes Level 1 learning assurance, explainability and ethics-based assessment plus Level 2 human-AI teaming and automated decisions under human oversight.
records.relevance_note: Direct aviation AI assurance and oversight guidance, and a distinct final version following the 2023 proposed Issue 2 consultation text.
remaining_checks: Re-open the official download after rate limiting clears and verify the cover date, exact issue notation, page count and any formal document identifier.
Model an explicit successor/final-version relationship to the proposed Issue 2 document and an implementation relationship to EASA AI Roadmap 2.0.

records.title: EASA Artificial Intelligence Concept Paper: Guidance for Level 1 & 2 machine learning applications — Proposed Issue 02
records.evidence_locator: Official general-publication page: exact proposed-version title and Publication Date 24/02/2023; linked consultation news describes a ten-week consultation and says the revision provides guidance for Level 1 and Level 2 safety-related AI systems, including human-AI teaming, human oversight, learning assurance, explainability and ethics-based assessment. EASA Roadmap 2.0 references this exact Proposed Issue 02 on printed p.34.
records.relevance_note: Independently citable consultation version in the aviation AI policy lineage; it must not be collapsed into the March 2024 final Issue 2.
remaining_checks: Re-open the official PDF after rate limiting clears and verify its cover date, page count and formal identifier.
Record consultation-to-final and Roadmap 2.0 implementation relationships without treating the versions as duplicate manifestations.

records.title: Draft reflection paper on the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the medicinal product lifecycle
records.evidence_locator: EMA guideline page, Document history: exact draft title and reference, consultation dates 19/07/2023-31/12/2023, First published 19/07/2023 and separate English PDF. Draft cover/adoption table identifies CHMP adoption for consultation on 10 July 2023 and CVMP adoption on 13 July 2023. Contents and sections 1-2 cover drug discovery, clinical trials, precision medicine, manufacturing, post-authorisation, model performance, interpretability, deployment, governance, data protection and trustworthy AI.
records.relevance_note: Substantive health-sector AI consultation text and a distinct predecessor version to the known September 2024 final reflection paper.
remaining_checks: Represent the later CVMP adoption on 13 July 2023 as an additional institutional date and preserve both committee roles.
Create an explicit draft-to-final version relationship to ema-ai-medicinal-product-lifecycle-reflection-paper-2024 if admitted.

records.title: Multi-annual AI workplan 2023-2028
records.document_date_note: The planned 14 December adoption meeting is not enough to establish the exact actual adoption date. Only December 2023 final adoption was confirmed in the evidence described here; document_date remains null.
records.evidence_locator: Official PDF, four workstreams: Guidance, policy and product support; Tools and technologies; Collaboration and change management; Experimentation. Printed p.8 identifies AI guidance for the medicines lifecycle, LLM guidance, preparation for the AI Act and creation of an AI Observatory. EMA news identifies joint HMA-EMA BDSG preparation and Management Board adoption; 30 October 2023 BDSG minutes state HMA endorsement was scheduled for 1 December and EMA Management Board adoption for 14 December 2023; later minutes confirm adoption by HMA and EMA in December 2023.
records.relevance_note: Joint multi-year operational AI policy for the European medicines regulatory network, distinct from the later NDSG 2026-2028 workplan already in the known backlog.
remaining_checks: Re-capture the English official news page's visible 18 December 2023 date header; the current English extractor omitted it although exact-page indexing and a saved render showed that date.

Verify the HMA endorsement date from final minutes before recording 1 December 2023 as an additional institutional date, and decide whether 14 December is adoption or endorsement in the canonical vocabulary.
Confirm no formal EMA reference appears in PDF metadata.

records.title: EBA Discussion Paper on machine learning for IRB models
records.evidence_locator: PDF cover: EBA/DP/2021/04 and 11 November 2021. Contents and executive summary, printed pp.5 and 9-24, address ML definitions, current use in credit-risk modelling, challenges/benefits, explainability and prudent use in IRB models. Official EBA publication/search record dates the document 11 November 2021 and the release text says EBA published it that day.
records.relevance_note: Direct banking-supervision AI/ML consultation document and the explicit precursor to the known 2023 follow-up report.
remaining_checks: Normalize the historically double-encoded official PDF URL without changing its identity, if the canonical source model requires a clean URL.
Record a consultation/predecessor relationship to eba-follow-up-machine-learning-irb-models-2023.

records.title: Public Statement: On the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the provision of retail investment services
records.evidence_locator: PDF cover and paras 1-3: 30 May 2024, ESMA35-335435667-5924, initial MiFID II guidance for firms using AI in retail investment services. Paras 5-24 cover hallucination, opacity, bias, data quality, human/management oversight, governance, testing, client disclosure, record keeping and staff competence. Official document record identifies type Statement and the same reference; release page dates and links it on 30/05/2024.
records.relevance_note: Direct, operative sectoral guidance on AI use by investment firms, not merely an AI market-monitoring study or press announcement.
remaining_checks: Editorially classify the Statement's policy tier and its relationship to the AI Act and MiFID II without implying that ESMA adopted the AI Act.

records.title: EIOPA's Report on the digitalisation of the European insurance sector
records.evidence_locator: PDF cover: EIOPA-BoS-24/139 and 30 April 2024; contents, section 3.1 Artificial Intelligence and section 3.1.2 AI Governance. Printed pp.3-4 and 22-29 report AI adoption rates, human oversight, high-impact approval, explainability, fairness, accountability, robustness and record keeping. Official publication page labels Publication date 30 April 2024 and links the English report.
records.relevance_note: Empirical EIOPA market-monitoring report with a substantial dedicated AI and AI-governance chapter; distinct from the known 2021 governance principles and 2025 opinion.
remaining_checks: Editorially decide whether the document's broader digitalisation scope satisfies the corpus centrality threshold; the dedicated AI/AI-governance chapter is substantive, not incidental.
Record contextual relationships to the 2019 thematic review and 2021 AI governance principles only if the canonical relationship vocabulary supports cited antecedents.

records.title: Factsheet on the regulatory framework applicable to AI systems in the insurance sector
records.evidence_locator: Official publication page labels Publication date 15 July 2024 and links the English two-page factsheet. PDF p.1 identifies life/health insurance pricing and risk-assessment AI as high-risk and summarises providers', deployers' and GPAI obligations; p.2 addresses market-surveillance authorities, sector-law overlap, governance, data, conformity assessment, transparency, incident response and outsourcing. Footer states EIOPA 2024 and that it is a preliminary informational overview.
records.relevance_note: Compact but directly substantive EIOPA mapping of the AI Act to insurance-sector regulation and supervision; distinct from the later governance opinion.
remaining_checks: Confirm whether the corpus admits short explanatory factsheets at the proposed policy tier; the document itself says it has no legal value.
Do not infer a formal document reference where none is visible.

records.title: EASA Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0: A human-centric approach to AI in aviation
records.evidence_locator: Known-backlog recheck. Official publication listing labels Publication Date 10/05/2023. PDF cover says May 2023, Version 2.0. Printed pp.6-7 define the expanded AI scope; pp.24-29 set the certification/guidance timeline, trustworthiness objectives and consolidated action plan; p.34 cites the proposed Issue 02 concept paper.
records.relevance_note: Confirmed substantive aviation AI roadmap and version identity; no match in the 131 canonical documents or corpus inventory, but already recorded in the 2026-09-05 gap backlog.
remaining_checks: Retain null document_date unless a distinct issue/adoption date is found; the cover month and official publication date do not establish a separate act date.
Record revision/successor relation to Roadmap 1.0 and implementation links to the proposed and final Issue 2 concept papers.

records.title: Reflection paper on the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the medicinal product lifecycle
records.evidence_locator: Known-backlog recheck. EMA page identifies the adopted current version, reference and First published 30/09/2024. PDF cover/adoption table gives MWP agreement 6 September, CHMP adoption 9 September and CVMP adoption 11 September 2024. Sections 1-2 and the detailed lifecycle/technical/governance sections make AI/ML the central regulatory subject.
records.relevance_note: Confirmed substantive final health-sector AI reflection paper and exact version/date distinction from its 2023 consultation draft.
remaining_checks: Preserve CHMP and CVMP as distinct adopter roles and dates; do not use the first committee date to erase the second.
Link explicitly to the 2023 draft version if both are admitted.

records.evidence_locator: Known-backlog recheck. Official EBA release is dated 4 August 2023, says EBA published the linked follow-up report that day, and describes feedback, current ML use cases, prudent IRB use, GDPR and AI Act interaction. Official search/library record dates the exact document 4 August 2023. Prior indexed PDF review recorded cover reference EBA/REP/2023/28 and substantive sections 4.3, 5.2 and Annex I.
records.relevance_note: Confirmed distinct follow-up/final report in the banking ML policy lineage, not a duplicate of the 2021 discussion paper.
remaining_checks: Re-open and locally verify the exact PDF cover and page locators when EBA's intermittent 403 response clears.
Record its response/successor relationship to EBA/DP/2021/04.

records.title: 2024 Coordinated Annual Review on Defence (CARD) report
records.evidence_locator: Known-backlog recheck. EDA CARD page says Ministers approved the report on 19 November 2024 and links the 14-page report; same-day EDA release identifies EDA as producer in coordination with EEAS and EUMS. PDF printed p.9, Research & Technology, has a dedicated Artificial Intelligence section on defence data spaces, testing, validation, certification and collaboration.
records.relevance_note: Confirmed substantive defence AI passage and institutional provenance, but this broader defence review was already in the 2026-09-05 backlog.
remaining_checks: Keep 19 November 2024 as adoption unless canonical review accepts the same-day official release linking the exact report as publication-manifestation evidence under section 5.1.
Do not infer joint authorship from EDA's statement that production was in coordination with EEAS and EUMS.
